source.title: Understanding SAE Features with the Logit Lens

record.tranche_reason: Measures the direct logit effects of learned SAE features in GPT-2 Small and reports whether those features align with interpretable token sets. This is indirect evidence relevant to V4, using logit-lens and enrichment measurements rather than testing superposition geometry.
record.gate_note: The post analyzes layer-8 GPT-2 Small SAE features using their decoder directions projected through the unembedding and token-set enrichment. It does not test superposition, feature sparsity or co-activity, interference, capacity competition, or neuron polysemanticity. It does not compare SAE features with ground-truth model features. The all-layer plots and scatterplots are linked, but the text does not give their numerical results; they are not transcribed as figure-only rows.
record.test_reason: The post takes GPT-2 Small layer-8 SAE features as given and proposes cheap tools for interpreting them: logit-weight statistics and token-set enrichment (TSEA). Its results are case studies of the tools on hand-picked features. It does not measure whether SAEs recover the model's features, how many features are interpretable, sparsity, spread across neurons, or anything about superposition. That is T4 rather than evidence on V4. The author's limitations say feature-class proportions and thresholds were not quantified.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct in substance. It is an informal methods post: logit-weight statistics and TSEA cheaply help interpret SAE features, but direct effects are incomplete, token sets can mislead, and prevalence across features, layers and models is unquantified.
record.recipe_differences: No superposition experiment or reproduction of the toy-model method. The post analyzes GPT-2 Small layer-8 SAE decoder features with logit-lens statistics and token-set enrichment.
record.method_sensitivity: Interpretation varies with the feature dashboard versus logit-weight or enrichment analysis, the token-set definitions and their quality, overlap among sets, and tokenization. The post does not quantify these sensitivities.

fits_no_version.finding: Layer-8 GPT-2 Small SAE features show distinct logit-weight distribution classes (partition, suppression, prediction, local context), analogous to universal neuron types. These are described qualitatively and unquantified.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAE features' direct output effects fall into classes analogous to neuron types (prediction, suppression, partition).

record.problems: Evidence is limited to GPT-2 Small layer-8 SAE features; feature-class prevalence and thresholds are not quantified. The author notes direct effects may not capture total effects, token-set results can be misleading, the NLTK tagger is imperfect, and tied embeddings complicate interpretation. The post does not establish feature recovery against ground truth or provide uncertainty estimates for the reported qualitative outcomes.
record.rows_left_out: The text links skewness/kurtosis plots for features and layers, but gives no numerical results in the post for those plots; these were not transcribed as figure-only rows. No results from cited prior work were included.

untested.parts: No toy model, sparsity transition or geometry.
No test of alternative causes of polysemanticity.
No measure of features spread across neurons, SAE sparsity, reconstruction, or recovery of model features. Interpretability of SAE features is assumed, not quantified.
No test of completeness, stability or canonicity.
No test of 1-D versus multi-dimensional features.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's supports and limits_scope labels on V4 are dropped. The post uses SAE features as a tool and evaluates its own interpretation method, so its rows do not bear on whether SAEs recover the model's sparse features.

versions.untested_parts: No toy-network experiment, sparsity-dependent transition, overlap geometry, or regular-geometry test.
No test of capacity pressure, feature competition, or dedicated versus shared dimensions.
No test of alternative causes of polysemantic neurons.

Does not test features spread across many neurons, feature firing sparsity, coverage or recovery against a ground truth, or whether the examined direct effects capture full feature function. Only GPT-2 Small layer 8 is analyzed.

Does not test feature completeness, stability, or canonical status. The author notes limitations of direct effects and gives examples where tokenization, overlapping sets, and tied embeddings complicate interpretation.
Does not compare one-dimensional directions with multidimensional feature representations.

rows.subject: GPT2 small
rows.operation_detail: Characterized layer-8 residual-stream SAE feature logit-weight distributions and associated token effects.
rows.measure: Logit-weight distribution; token effects described for this feature class.
rows.value: Features with high kurtosis and low standard deviation generally promote specific tokens or small token sets; noticeable outliers often correspond to bracket-closing or quote-closing tokens.
rows.locator: Characterizing Features via the Logit Weight Distribution — Local Context Features
rows.note: Qualitative characterization; the post does not report the fraction of features in this class.
rows.check: Qualitative description of a feature class found with the post's own method. It does not measure whether SAEs recover model features (V4).

rows.subject: GPT2 small
rows.operation_detail: Characterized layer-8 residual-stream SAE feature logit-weight distributions and associated token effects.
rows.measure: Logit-weight distribution; token effects described for this feature class.
rows.value: Prototypical partition features are described as cleanly bimodal; the modes correspond to combinations of whether the next token starts with a space and whether it is capitalized. The characterization also gives higher standard deviation, right skewness, and low kurtosis.
rows.locator: Characterizing Features via the Logit Weight Distribution — Partition Features
rows.note: The author says boundaries between feature classes are not established and does not quantify prevalence.
rows.check: Partition-feature characterization from the method. No prevalence or recovery measure.

rows.subject: GPT2 small
rows.operation_detail: Characterized layer-8 residual-stream SAE feature logit-weight distributions and associated token effects.
rows.measure: Logit-weight distribution; promoted token sets described for this feature class.
rows.value: Features described as having high skewness and standard deviation between 0.03 and 0.07; examples of promoted sets include numerical digits, all-caps tokens, and verbs of a particular form.
rows.locator: Characterizing Features via the Logit Weight Distribution — Prediction Features
rows.note: Qualitative examples, not an estimate of the share or completeness of such features.
rows.check: Prediction-feature characterization. The 0.03–0.07 std is a selection criterion, not a result on V4.

rows.subject: GPT2 small
rows.operation_detail: Characterized layer-8 residual-stream SAE feature logit-weight distributions and associated token effects.
rows.measure: Logit-weight distribution; suppressed token sets described for this feature class.
rows.value: Features with negative skew and low kurtosis are described as potentially suppressing sets of tokens. The author says there may not be a clear boundary from context-specific partition features.
rows.locator: Characterizing Features via the Logit Weight Distribution — Suppression Features
rows.check: Tentative suppression-feature class description. Not a V4 measure.

rows.subject: GPT2 small
rows.operation_detail: Applied token-set enrichment to regex-defined token categories across SAE features.

conditions.value: Starts with space; starts with a capital letter; all digits; punctuation; all capital letters

rows.value: The author reports a fairly strong token-set effect: some tested sets achieved generally higher enrichment scores than others.
rows.locator: Token Set Enrichment Analysis — Regex Sets
rows.note: No threshold for significance is proposed; the author says the results need further interpretation.
rows.check: Reports the TSEA method's own behaviour (a set effect) on the top 5000 features by skewness, with no threshold. This is method performance.

rows.subject: GPT2 small
rows.operation_detail: Applied token-set enrichment to NLTK part-of-speech token categories across SAE features.

conditions.value: VBN, VBG, VB, VBD verb categories

rows.value: The author reports a token-set effect for the verb sets, but notes that base-form verbs did not show higher enrichment than other, smaller verb sets; the reason is uncertain.
rows.locator: Token Set Enrichment Analysis — NLTK Sets: Starting with a Space, or a Capital Letter
rows.note: The post flags limitations of the tagger and possible tokenization effects.
rows.check: TSEA method behaviour on NLTK verb sets. Not a measure of superposition or SAE recovery.

rows.subject: GPT2 small
rows.operation_detail: Compared token-set enrichment for boys' and girls' name sets across SAE features.

conditions.value: 300 most common boys' names versus 300 most common girls' names

rows.measure: Enrichment scores for the two name sets.
rows.value: Some features score highly for both sets; the plot has more features in the girls'-name-specific top-left region than in the boys'-name-specific bottom-right region.
rows.locator: Token Set Enrichment Analysis — Arbitrary Sets: Boys Names and Girls Names
rows.note: The author cautions that enrichment results can be misleading because of related or incomplete sets and the tied embedding.
rows.check: TSEA scatter for name sets. Method demonstration only.

rows.subject: GPT2 small
rows.operation_detail: Inspected layer-8 SAE feature 89's logit-weight distribution and activation examples against token-set enrichment.
rows.measure: Token-set enrichment and direct logit effects for the all-caps category.
rows.value: The dashboard suggested promotion of two capital-character tokens beginning with a space, while the logit-weight distribution and enrichment result suggested promotion of many all-caps tokens; activation examples were described as supporting the broader category.
rows.note: The discrepancy between dashboard interpretation and the broader token-set result shows that feature interpretation depends on the measurement used.
rows.check: Single-feature case study (feature 89) comparing the dashboard with TSEA. Method validation.

rows.subject: GPT2 small
rows.operation_detail: Inspected layer-8 SAE feature 5382's logit-weight distribution against NLTK verb-set labels.
rows.measure: Token-set enrichment and direct logit effects for the verb category.
rows.value: The feature appeared to promote verbs ending in “ing”; the author attributes distribution overlap to NLTK mislabeling tokens such as “Viking,” “Ring,” and “String.”
rows.note: The interpretation depends on imperfect token labels.

rows.subject: GPT2 small
rows.operation_detail: Inspected layer-8 SAE feature 18006's token-set enrichment and logit effects.

conditions.value: VBN past participles and VBD past-tense verbs

rows.measure: Token-set enrichment and direct logit effects for two related verb categories.
rows.value: The feature appeared to promote tokens in both past-tense verb and past-participle sets; the author notes that the sets overlap and that this can make enrichment misleading.
rows.note: The post does not further distinguish tokens unique to each set.
rows.check: Single-feature case study (feature 18006). Method caveat about overlapping sets.

rows.subject: GPT2 small
rows.operation_detail: Inspected layer-8 SAE feature 2896's logit effects, name-set enrichment, and activation examples.

conditions.value: 300 most common boys' names and girls' names

rows.measure: Name-set enrichment and direct positive and negative logit effects.
rows.value: Although enrichment suggested promotion of boys' names over girls' names, inspection suggested a broader gender-related feature: elevated tokens included titles such as “Mr” and less common boys' names, while the top negative logits were described as female-oriented. The author also thought it often fired on punctuation after a male pronoun.
rows.locator: Arbitrary Sets: Boys Names and Girls Names — Feature 2896
rows.note: The author describes the feature interpretation as more nuanced than the enrichment result and presents the activation interpretation tentatively.

rows.subject: GPT2 small
rows.operation_detail: Inspected layer-8 SAE feature 18206's logit effects and activation examples against the girls'-name set.
rows.measure: Girls'-name enrichment and direct logit effects.
rows.value: The feature appeared to promote common girls' names and additional girls' names outside the top 300. It was described as firing especially strongly on the second token of some tokenized female names; the author says the mechanism is unclear given GPT-2's tied embedding.
rows.locator: Arbitrary Sets: Boys Names and Girls Names — Feature 18206
rows.note: The post notes tokenization and tied-embedding complications.
rows.check: Single-feature case study (feature 18206). Method caveat about tied embeddings.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: GPT-2 Small layer-8 SAE features and the reported token categories
reader_labels.reason: The post reports SAE features whose direct logit effects align with interpretable token sets, including all-caps tokens, verbs, and names (r1-r12). This is indirect evidence from one model and layer.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Interpretation of the measured features and enrichment results
reader_labels.reason: The examples include mismatches or ambiguities involving dashboards, imperfect token labels, overlapping sets, tokenization, tied embeddings, and direct effects that may not capture total feature effects (r6,r8-r12).
